title: Critical Evaluation of the Golden Ratio and Its Applications in Meaningful Logo Design and Global Brand Management
content: The uncontested preeminence of the golden ratio (ϕ) has come to occupy a central role in aesthetics and graphic design due to its uncanny appeal to the human eye. This ratio represents an irrational number and has been called the divine proportion for its uncanny presence and applications in the natural world. Hence, this paper critically reevaluates the status of the golden ratio as the secret to innate design and composition. Academic literature has a bifurcation that either supports or suppresses the golden ratio, and studies several of its features and effects in abstract isolation. This paper discusses various arguments to reveal the true nature of the divine proportion. The findings contribute to comprehending parallel proportions like 1:1 and 1:√2 as effective substitutes, creating unexplored and unconsidered avenues for cultural coherence and formulating an aligned brand identity. To resolve the chasm between standardisation and localisation of corporations, this article proposes a modular arrangement of multi-media assets that cater to a wide-ranging audience. This paper also portrays a blueprint to coalesce developments in artificial intelligence and generative technologies, and the golden ratio, into precise logo creation and global brand management. This integrative literature review has sought to validate or pierce the praised reputation of the divine ratio in the figurative blueprint for extralimital design. The future of global brand management relies entirely on extracting an equilibrium between a recognisable market face and user-tailored purposeful design, and treating context-specific malleability as the roadmap to an eclectic audience.
